assumptions: Paragraph 10 is read with the supplied ownership-record requirement and paragraph 14 assurance provisions.
Operational evidence is assessed against an applicable standard, rather than an invented guarantee against every failure.

citations.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement1.

1 Given that these tokenised products are offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of maintaining proper records to reflect investors’ ownership, the Product Provider should remain fully responsible, despite any outsourcing arrangement such as those envisaged under 6.8 of the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds. For factors of consideration, please also refer to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable, when formulating the tokenisation arrangement.

Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained and the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with service providers involved2.

Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

17. Where intermediaries deal in, advise on, or manage portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities, intermediaries are reminded to conduct due diligence on the issuers and their third-party vendors/service providers involved in the tokenisation arrangement as well as the features and risks arising from the tokenisation arrangement. 18. Intermediaries should understand and be satisfied with the controls implemented by the issuers and their third-party vendors/service providers to manage ownership and technology risks of the Tokenised Securities before they engage in related activities. Please refer to Parts A and B of the Appendix to this circular for a non-exhaustive list of factors for consideration.

node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.distinction: This reading makes substantive performance part of fulfillment of the responsibility requirement itself. Under the allocation reading, retained responsibility can be established separately from failed performance; here, authority and diligent supervision alone cannot establish fulfillment where required outcomes are absent.
questions: How does the applicable standard treat an incident despite diligent supervision, including materiality and remediation?
What evidence establishes operational compatibility, accurate ownership records and the other referenced requirements?
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.statement: Read with the express requirement to ensure proper ownership records and operational compatibility, paragraph 10 can instead be understood as requiring the Product Provider to discharge substantive responsibility for the arrangement. A supported fulfillment conclusion would require evidence of retained accountability, effective supervisory conduct and operational and record-keeping performance meeting the applicable standard. Formal authority or an assertion of responsibility is insufficient; supervision is evidence of performance, not an automatic substitute for it. The intermediary due-diligence and prior satisfaction provisions concern separate actors and controls and cannot themselves establish provider fulfillment. The excerpt does not resolve whether every failure defeats fulfillment or whether an applicable standard permits a qualified assessment.
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.subject: Paragraph 10 and footnote 1: substantive discharge of responsibility

node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.question: Has the Product Provider substantively discharged paragraph 10 responsibility through retained accountability, effective supervisory conduct and satisfactory operational and record-keeping performance under the applicable standard?
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.unit_of_assessment: One Product Provider's substantive responsibility for one tokenisation arrangement and its ownership records.
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.temporal_basis: The period assessed for continuing responsibility; treatment of incident materiality, duration and remediation remains unspecified.
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.true_means: Substantive fulfillment is established under the candidate's reading, including the relevant proper-records and compatibility outcomes. Formal authority or supervision alone is insufficient. Separate intermediary due-diligence and prior-control-satisfaction duties do not establish provider fulfillment.
node.05b977f28b68c771dbfcd320.false_means: The substantive responsibility requirement fails under the applicable standard. A particular incident does not automatically establish failure without that standard; missing evidence leaves the answer unresolved.
